feedback: If the child can't locate the spine, guide their hand down the centre of the back to feel the bumpy line.
Confirm each match: 'Yes — that hard part is your ribcage, caging your heart and lungs.'
activities.intendedInsight: The bones you can feel on your own body are the same frame shown in the picture, and they shield the soft parts inside.
learnerActions: Press the top and back of your head to feel the hard skull; run your fingers down the middle of your back to feel the spine; press the front of your chest to feel the ribs.
Match each hard part you feel to the same part on the picture.
Say which soft organ each hard part is guarding (skull→brain, ribs→heart and lungs).
activities.title: Feel your own frame

feedback: A full answer explains support/protection (naming an organ shielded) AND that muscles pull on bones to move them, using the boneless animal to justify why we need a frame.
If the child gives only one half (shape/protection OR movement), ask the missing part directly.
If the child says muscles push, re-establish that muscles only pull (tighten and shorten).
activities.intendedInsight: The skeleton is needed for firm shape, support and protection of soft organs, and movement comes from muscles pulling on bones.
learnerActions: Think about a jellyfish, which has no bones at all.

Say what a jellyfish can't do that you can because you have a skeleton (for example, stand up tall on land or keep its shape out of water) — remembering that a jellyfish can still swim using its muscles.
Answer the two-part question: why do you have a hard skeleton inside you, and when you bend your arm to lift a cup, what makes the arm actually move?
activities.title: Boneless-animal reasoning check

feedback: If the match is wrong, return to the labelled figure or the child's own body to re-feel and re-name the part.
If 'push' is chosen, re-establish that muscles only pull.
activities.intendedInsight: Consolidate bone names, what each protects, and that muscles pull.
learnerActions: Match each bone to the organ it protects (skull→brain, ribcage→heart and lungs).
Answer the quick question: do muscles push or pull to move bones?
activities.title: Optional: match and quick-check
